weeks.theme: This week the focus is on dribbling, and specifically escaping the pressure from a defender.
weeks.goal: We will focus on teaching three skill moves. By the end of the week all players must know how to do them.
weeks.seasonFocus: We start with basic moves to beat a defender. By the end of the season we want every player to master every one of these skill moves.

logistics: Watch the short videos at the bottom of the page so you know how to demonstrate. Each video is just a few seconds.
I strongly recommend that you print the exercises for each day on paper, so it is easier for you to refer to it on the field.

STAY WITH YOUR PLAYERS UNTIL ALL OF THEM ARE PICKED UP. Do not leave any players unattended at the fields. Coaches are responsible for all players under their care, even if you are coaching players from another team.
Study the practice sessions in advance and know the instructions and coaching points. You can refer to it during practices to make sure you are

As always, adjust the practice variables to make the exercise work for your players, based on their level of ability, age, size, numbers, etc. See the attached Manipulating Practice Variables document (Tom Turner, OYSAN Director of Coaching and Player Development), and study it.

coachingNotes.title: Demonstration-Observation-Correction Cycle
points: You must demonstrate each skill move to your players, and then have them repeat them 20 times.
Do not talk while demonstrating. Just do the skill move yourself at game speed, with no talking. Just do the move like you want them to do it in a game situation.
Have the players repeat it 20 times and observe them. Players sit down when done.
Demonstrate again – do it at speed. Then break it down into its two or three component parts. Here you can explain each part, but be brief.
Have the players repeat the skill move 20 times and sit down when done.

So the process is as follows: demonstrate, observe the players, demonstrate again to make corrections, observe the players, and repeat this process until the players' performance improves. Not all players will master every move on the first session. It will take several sessions.
Repeat this for each skill move.
Work on five or six skill moves each practice session, and make sure the players are using those specific moves in the exercise progression for that day.
Our objective is for all players, regardless of their athletic ability, to master every one of these skill moves.

coachingNotes.title: Session Model
points: We are using a progression model for our practice sessions. We will not use the Play-Practice-Play session model, so don't use that. You can still apply the guided discovery technique within the progression model.

coachingNotes.title: Cycle of Possession
points: Most of these are possession games, and you must focus your coaching points on dribbling to escape the pressure from a defender, so you create enough time and space to make a safe pass or to get a shot.

You should all start introducing your players to the four stages of the cycle of possession (1 - pop away from the defender to create time and space, 2- good first touch when you receive the ball, 3 - escape the pressure to create time and space to pass, 4 - accurate pass to the feet, and repeat the entire sequence).

coachingNotes.title: Technique Coaching Points
points: Players must use the correct technique when receiving or dribbling: take small soft touches. Quick feet and small steps so you can react quickly. Dribble side to side, not forward into pressure. Always be aware what spaces the defenders are taking away and what spaces they are giving you. Take what they give you. Shield the ball when necessary.

Players must use the correct technique when passing (contact the ball with the inside of the heel, push through the ball and swing the kicking leg up – do not jab at the ball, or jab your kicking foot into the ground).

Players must use the correct technique when receiving the ball – small touch so you can play it immediately. Use the correct surface of the foot – inside of the heel, or sole of the foot if you are in a tight space.

2v2-game.title: 2V2 Game
2v2-game.setup: 20X30 yard area (adjust for your age group)
instructions: The coach passes to the far corner. The receiver dribbles diagonally, and his team mate overlaps. Two defender come in. Play is continuous until the ball is out of bounds. Goalies are not allowed to punt or shoot.
coachingPoints: Dribble diagonally to create time and space. Pass early. Shoot early. Quick transitions to defense and to offense.
Look to combine with give-&-gos, overlaps, and through balls.
Be aware what the defender is taking away and what he is giving you. Take what he gives you.

basic-ball-skills.title: Basic Ball Skills
basic-ball-skills.setup: Individual ball skills – Open area or 20x20 yard area, no need to use a line of cones. The coach demonstrates each move, players repeat it 10 times. Note that in the videos linked some of the moves are given a different name. A rose by any other name… Spend 10 minutes on this. If you do all the list below it will take you more than an hour… After players learn all the moves they can do more of them inside of 10 minutes.
instructions: Full circle, 360 degrees circle (three touches is enough to do a full circle; chop the ball around using the inside of the foot, then outside of the foot, then repeat with the other foot) ten times
Side step https://youtu.be/-pwFS7tg16E
Scissors – ten times https://youtu.be/QpLPYdHlGGs
Step-Overs – ten times https://youtu.be/cldbJhHK0Ks
Cruyff https://youtu.be/RQFs_no6MGs
Twist (shimmy) – ten times https://youtu.be/0fQx2l8Q_uM
Pull-push https://youtu.be/mB0G4lHSSyI
Pull-cut https://youtu.be/-dNzgYSBQi8
Hook turn (called U turn in the video) https://youtu.be/n4FaeICzPtM
Drag back – 180 degree turn, drag ball straight back using sole of foot, turn body right if using right foot, left if using left foot
Maradona – ten times https://youtu.be/DzbdeHLbxwg
Sole delay (and pop away to the side) – ten times https://youtu.be/IlgdHkqkzjI
coachingPoints: These points refer to when and why players must each of these skill moves in a game: to create time and space for themselves and escape the pressure from a defender.

Any time you have the ball there will be a defender right in front of you. You must dribble to the side in order to escape the pressure. There are four basic ways to do this: cut to the side, turn and face away, sole delay, and skill moves. Choose the right way depending on how close the defender is to you.
If you have lots of space between you and the defender: use skill moves like the scissors or step-overs

If you have a couple yards between you and the defender: use the twist, pull-push, pull-cut, sole delay, Maradona. But the fastest and safest way to escape pressure in this situation is a simple cut to the side.
If the defender is really close you must TURN AND FACE AWAY immediately. Use the inside cut, Cruyff, hook turn, or dragback

dribbling-four-goals.title: Dribbling - Four Goals
instructions: The coach plays a diagonal ball toward the far goal. The attacker runs behind the far goal. The defender runs behind the near goal. Switch roles after all players have gone a turn.
1: Score by dribbling through.
2: Score by shooting.
coachingPoints: Attackers: Get to the ball first. Take a first touch toward one of the goals to make the defender commit to that goal. Then quickly turn and attack the opposite goal.

Defenders: Get to the ball as quickly as possible to deny the shot. Don't stab at it, or dive in. Instead, delay the attack by staying on your toes and shuffling to keep the ball in front of you. Be patient and wait for the attacker to make a mistake. If you win the ball counterattack quickly.

dribbling-gauntlet.title: Dribbling Gauntlet

diagram.extractedFrom: page-1 FlateDecode /Image XObject (raw pixels, re-packed as PNG)

dribbling-gauntlet.setup: 10X36 yard area, divided into three 10X12 sections. Three defenders, and a line of attackers.
instructions: One attacker dribbles through and scores by dribbling past the last end line. On the way the attacker must beat each defender.

Defenders must start at the back line of their respective squares. Defenders are not allowed outside their respective squares. Defenders score by winning the ball and stopping the ball dead on the front line of their square.
coachingPoints: Dribble with shoelaces to take on defenders. Make your move early, out of the defender's reach.
Change direction, and accelerate away.
Attack the spaces behind the defender with speed.
Control the ball again when you enter the next square.

dribbling-multiple-gates.title: Dribbling - Multiple Gates
dribbling-multiple-gates.setup: 30X40 area (adjust to your # of players and age). Multiple "gates" made with cones.
instructions: Play multiple 1V1 battles. Dribbler scores by dribbling through gates. Defender must deny the dribble through the gates, but cannot steal the ball. Play 1 or 2 minutes, and switch roles. Keep score.
Variation 2: Defenders can win the ball. Keep score.
coachingPoints: Take soft short touches, keeping the ball "tied" to your feet. Quick choppy steps, with constant changes of direction.
The objective is to be unpredictable and to move the ball before the defender can react.
Make the defender commit to defend one gate, and immediately change directions to another gate.
Use every surface of both feet.

derived.areaSize: 30x40 yards (adjust to # of players and age)

multiple-1v1s-dribble-pass.title: Multiple 1v1s - Dribble-Pass
multiple-1v1s-dribble-pass.setup: 20x20 or 20x30 area. Two teams. Target players for each team on opposite sides, multiple 1v1 pairs inside.
instructions: Players keep the ball away from the defender, and pass to the target player outside. The target player and the passer switch positions and the defender keeps following the same ball.
coachingPoints: Player with the ball: Never face the defender - turn and dribble out. Pass early. Accurate passes to the feet. Call out the target's name to make sure she is ready.
Target: Good first touch into open space. Accelerate away and pass to the target player on the opposite side. Pass from a distance, so you don't bring the defender close to the target.

possession-knockout-game.title: Possession Knockout Game
instructions: Team in possession has two or three balls. Two "sharks" go after the ball. You can stipulate that the sharks cannot double team.
coachingPoints: Escape the pressure from the defender quickly. Pass early. Accurate passes to the feet.
Players off the ball must create time and space.
